info.title: D-Human app API
info.description: The routes the native apps use. Every answer is private, no-store, except POST /api/auth/code's (the web's route, unchanged). Only a 401 means signed out: a missing, malformed, expired or revoked token. Every other /api route answers a live token with 403 not_for_app (it isn't open to the apps yet): keep the sign-in. Errors are { error, message? }. Requests with Authorization must not carry Origin or Sec-Fetch-* headers.

post.summary: Email a 6-digit sign-in code, then exchange it at POST /api/auth/token. The web's own route, unchanged: no token needed, and its answers carry no Cache-Control.

parameters.name: X-DHuman-Client
parameters.description: ios/1.0.0 (42). Used only for update prompts.

code.description: Six digits, or the App Review account's 20 or more. Spaces and dashes are ignored.

key.description: A new random key for each try, at least 128 bits (a UUIDv4 is fine); never a device id, a counter or anything reused. Send it again with a resend: the same email, code and key within 10 minutes get the same token, even after the code is used, so the key must be as secret as the code.

label.description: The hardware model, e.g. iPhone18,1. Never the phone's name.

token.description: Shown once. Keep it in the Keychain; send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

expiresAt.description: 90 days after last use, at most 365 days after sign-in. Use slides it.
